Swedish Government Announces $747 Million Package for Businesses Ahead of 2026 Election

  • by Lauren Jacobs
  • 10th September 2025

Sweden's government plans a 7 billion crown ($747 million) package in the 2026 budget to support small businesses, boost jobs, and spur economic growth.

The Swedish government unveiled a 7 billion crown ($747 million) package in its 2026 budget aimed at supporting small businesses and stimulating job growth ahead of the election year. Deputy Prime Minister Ebba Busch said the measures will benefit 60,000 small businesses through tax reductions, temporary incentives to hire young workers, and efforts to cut red tape for more profitable operations. The broader minority right-wing coalition budget includes an 80 billion crown boost to the economy, featuring income tax cuts, electricity tax reductions, and lower VAT on food. Officials say the full budget will be presented on September 22. The government emphasized its goal of making Sweden a country where it is easy to start and grow a company, aiming to create a more dynamic business environment and encourage entrepreneurship.
